claims.claim: Queen Victoria had her children's heads read by a phrenologist
claims.quote: Phrenology was not limited to the common people, and both Queen Victoria and Prince Albert invited George Combe to read the heads of their children.

claims.claim: Queen Victoria and Prince Albert together invited George Combe to examine their children
claims.quote: both Queen Victoria and Prince Albert invited George Combe to read the heads of their children

claims.claim: George Combe was the era's chief promoter of phrenology
claims.quote: George Combe would become the chief promoter of phrenology throughout the English-speaking world after he viewed a brain dissection by Spurzheim, convincing him of phrenology's merits.

claims.claim: The bust pictured is an L. N. Fowler phrenology bust held by the Whipple Museum
claims.quote: Archive title: File:Lorenzo Fowler - Phrenology bust - Whipple Wh.2744.jpg

claims.claim: The bust is lettered 'PHRENOLOGY BY L.N.FOWLER'
claims.quote: PHRENOLOGY BY L.N.FOWLER.

claims.claim: Combe's phrenology book sold 200,000 copies
claims.quote: George Combe's book On the Constitution of Man and its Relationship to External Objects sold more than 200,000 copies through nine editions.

claims.claim: The book's title was 'On the Constitution of Man'
claims.quote: George Combe's book On the Constitution of Man and its Relationship to External Objects sold more than 200,000 copies through nine editions.

claims.claim: Scientific lectures were a form of middle-class entertainment
claims.quote: Phrenology's success was also partly because it was introduced at a time when scientific lectures were becoming a form of middle-class entertainment

claims.claim: By the 1840s London had over 28 phrenological societies
claims.quote: By the 1840s there were more than 28 phrenological societies in London with more than 1,000 members.

claims.claim: The journal cover shown is the American Phrenological Journal of March 1848
claims.quote: Description: Cover of American Phrenological Journal from March 1848, volume 10, number 3

claims.claim: Gall divided the brain into 27 organs
claims.quote: Franz Joseph Gall believed that the brain was made up of 27 individual organs that determined personality

claims.claim: Phrenologists never agreed on the number of organs, which drifted from 27 to over 40
claims.quote: Phrenologists had never been able to agree on the most basic mental organ numbers, going from 27 to over 40, and had difficulty locating the mental organs.

claims.claim: Phrenologists struggled to locate the organs
claims.quote: had difficulty locating the mental organs

claims.claim: The skull shown was annotated by Pastor Oberlin according to Gall's system, and is at Waldersbach
claims.quote: Crâne humain annoté par le pasteur Oberlin selon le système de Franz Joseph Gall (phrénologie) - Musée Jean-Frédéric Oberlin à Waldersbach (67)

claims.claim: People consulted phrenologists about hiring staff and choosing spouses
claims.quote: People also consulted phrenologists for advice in matters such as hiring personnel or finding suitable marriage partners.

claims.claim: The phrenologist ran fingertips and palms over the skull
claims.quote: Phrenologists would run their fingertips and palms over the skulls of their patients to feel for enlargements or indentations.

claims.claim: Clients were issued a written character delineation
claims.quote: After such an examination, clients received a written delineation of their character or a standardized chart with their score, combined with advice on how to improve themselves.

claims.claim: The illustration is A. S. Hartrick's 'The Phrenologist', 1895
claims.quote: Archive title: File:The Phrenologist.jpg ... Date: 1895 ... Author: Archibald Standish Hartrick OBE RWS

claims.claim: In 1927 an incoming member of the US Congress had his skull measured
claims.quote: De schedelmeting bij een komend lid van het Amerikaanse Congres, in het kader van een psycho-fysiek [antropologisch] onderzoek dat zij moeten ondergaan voordat zij zitting nemen, Verenigde Staten van Amerika, 1927.

claims.claim: Phrenology as a theory died in the 1840s
claims.quote: Phrenology was mostly discredited as a scientific theory by the 1840s.

claims.claim: Skull-measuring instruments continued in use after phrenology ended
claims.quote: In general, instruments to measure sizes of cranium continued to be used after the mainstream phrenology had ended.

claims.claim: In 1930s Rwanda, Belgian colonial officials used phrenology to rank Tutsi above Hutu
claims.quote: During the 1930s, Belgian colonial authorities in Rwanda used phrenology to explain the purported superiority of Tutsis over Hutus.

claims.claim: Skull shape predicts nothing about personality or mental traits
claims.quote: The central phrenological notion that measuring the contour of the skull can predict personality traits is discredited by empirical research.

claims.claim: Flourens' ablation work and Broca's speech area had dismantled phrenology by 1840
claims.quote: Between Flourens and Broca, the claims to support phrenology were dismantled.

claims.claim: Gall's correct insight was that the brain is spatially organised, with a real division of labour
claims.quote: He contributed to the idea that the brain is spatially organized, but not in the way he proposed. There is a clear division of labor in the brain but none of which even remotely correlates to the size of the head or the structure of the skull.

claims.claim: The lecture poster is by Samuel Robert Wells, 1875
claims.quote:
Date: 1875
Author: Samuel Robert Wells

claims.claim: Phrenology counted as respectable science roughly from 1810 to 1840
claims.quote: the discipline was influential in the 19th century, especially from about 1810 until 1840

claims.claim: Franz Joseph Gall began lecturing in 1796
claims.quote: In 1796 the German physician Franz Joseph Gall (1758–1828) began lecturing on organology: the isolation of mental faculties and later cranioscopy

claims.claim: Gall held that the brain was an aggregate of organs whose size was impressed on the overlying skull
claims.quote: It was believed that the cranial skull—like a glove on the hand—accommodates to the different sizes of these areas of the brain, so that a person's capacity for a given personality trait could be determined simply by measuring the area of the skull that overlies the corresponding area of the brain.

claims.claim: Contemporaries in the 19th century already called phrenology pseudoscience
claims.quote: The methodological rigor of phrenology was doubtful even for the standards of its time, since many authors already regarded phrenology as pseudoscience in the 19th century.

claims.claim: Pierre Flourens removed parts of pigeons' brains and found the losses did not match Gall's map
claims.quote: Jean Pierre Flourens' experiments on the brains of pigeons indicated that the loss of parts of the brain either caused no loss of function, or the loss of a completely different function than what had been attributed to it by phrenology.

claims.claim: Paul Broca found a left frontal lesion that destroyed speech production but left comprehension intact
claims.quote: the patient's ability to produce language was lost while their ability to understand language remained intact, due to a lesion on the left frontal lobe

claims.claim: Phrenology was used to rank races
claims.quote: By comparing skulls of different ethnic groups it was thought to allow for ranking of races from least to most evolved.

claims.claim: The Fowler bust is made of china
claims.quote: gained considerable fame with his phrenology head (a china head showing the phrenological faculties), which has become a symbol of the discipline
